test_intent: Verify that a valid command text routes to the matching ICommandHandler and returns true, while other handlers are not invoked.
reason: Clean unit test at the correct seam. Mock verify assertions confirm both positive (correct handler called once) and negative (other handler never called) outcomes. State assertion on return value complements mock verification. Low maintenance risk, focused scope.

test_intent: Verify that an unrecognized command name returns false and no handler is invoked.
reason: Clean unit test at the correct seam. Verifies the negative path: unknown commands are rejected without invoking any handler. Complements the positive routing test. Low maintenance risk.

test_intent: Verify that a message that does not start with / is not treated as a command and returns false.
reason: Clean unit test at the correct seam. Verifies the non-command guard path in the router. Completes the trio of routing tests (valid, unknown, non-command). Low maintenance risk.

test_intent: Verify that a second registered command routes to its corresponding handler, confirming multi-handler routing works.
reason: Clean unit test at the correct seam. Confirms the router iterates through all registered handlers and matches the correct one, not just the first. Low maintenance risk.

test_intent: Verify that CommandsModule.AddCommandsServices registers the expected set of command handlers and services into the DI container.
reason: DI registration smoke test. Verifies service descriptors exist after calling the module method. No distinct bot contract beyond compile-time registration coverage. If a handler is removed or renamed, the build or runtime will fail anyway. The test is brittle because it depends on the exact set of registered types and requires many mocks to be set up. No replacement needed.

test_intent: Verify that AddConfigurationServices returns the same ServiceCollection instance (fluent API pattern).
reason: Tests the .NET fluent extension method convention (returning the same ServiceCollection). This is a framework pattern, not a bot contract. The sibling test AddConfigurationServices_ShouldRegisterIAppConfig in the same file already covers the meaningful behavior. Deleting this test has zero risk and removes noise.

test_intent: Verify that EnsureChatAsync adds a new chat to the statistics store without throwing.
reason: Current test uses Assert.Pass after calling the method, which only verifies no exception was thrown. The comment admits state cannot be checked because data is saved to a file. The behavior (chat registration in stats) is a real bot contract worth testing. Rewrite to assert on observable state: verify GetChatMemberCount was called on the mock, or verify file I/O side effects, or test the in-memory state before persistence.

test_intent: Verify that calling EnsureChatAsync on an existing chat updates its title.
reason: Current test uses Assert.Pass after calling the method twice, providing no assertion about whether the title was actually updated. The behavior (updating existing chat metadata) is a real contract. Rewrite to assert on observable state: verify the chat's title changed in the in-memory store or persisted data, or verify the mock was called with expected parameters.
